headline: Woman dies after officer-involved shooting during Bath pursuit
dek: The shooting followed a pursuit that ended near the Route 302 and Route 112 junction. New Hampshire investigators have not said who fired the shots or identified the woman.
body: A woman died Thursday evening after an officer-involved shooting in Bath, New Hampshire, following a pursuit that ended near the intersection of Routes 302 and 112. The New Hampshire attorney general’s office said state troopers and a local police officer were trying to locate a vehicle that had been sought earlier in the day when it stopped in the Grafton County town.

According to the attorney general’s account, the officers made contact with a woman who appeared to be holding a handgun. Shots were fired during the interaction, and the woman was injured. She was taken to an area hospital and later pronounced dead. The woman’s name had not been released as of Friday afternoon, and authorities had not identified the troopers or local officer involved.

The initial official account does not establish who fired the shots. New Hampshire Public Radio, reporting with the Caledonian Record, said the attorney general’s office and the State Police Major Crime Unit are investigating. [Boston 25 News](https://www.boston25news.com/news/local/woman-dead-after-pursuit-officer-involved-shooting-new-hampshire-ag-says/KZWBX46NI5D4XNOOEDHDISOAQA/), [NBC Boston](https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/woman-killed-in-police-shooting-in-bath-nh/4028447/) and [the Boston Globe](https://www.bostonglobe.com/2026/10/08/metro/bath-nh-fatal-police-shooting/) separately reported the same basic sequence from the attorney general’s statement: a vehicle pursuit, contact with an apparently armed woman, gunfire, a hospital transport and a death.

[NHPR](https://www.nhpr.org/nh-news/2026-10-09/woman-dies-police-shooting-bath-nh-newhampshire) also reported that police radio transmissions and a statewide alert described a child-custody dispute and threats attributed to the woman before officers located the vehicle. The alert said she was believed to have a firearm and might be traveling toward her mother’s home in Bath. Those statements are part of the information investigators were working with; they are not a public finding that the woman committed a crime, and the circumstances behind the alert had not been fully explained.

The pursuit covered several North Country roads before the shooting. NHPR reported that officers tracked the vehicle north on Interstate 93 near Thornton, then followed its path along Lost River Road through Woodstock and west on Route 112 toward Bath. A police transmission indicated that the driver had crossed the center line, and officers arranged to deploy spike strips near the Routes 112 and 302 junction. The vehicle stopped near a campground after striking the strips, according to the radio traffic described by NHPR.

The moments immediately after the stop remain unsettled. Dispatch traffic reported gunfire and an injured woman, but did not determine whether her wound was self-inflicted, according to NHPR’s account. Officials have not publicly said how many shots were fired, whether the woman discharged the handgun, or which officer—or officers—used a firearm. No other civilians or law-enforcement personnel were physically injured, and the attorney general’s office said there was no known continuing threat to the public.

Bath is a small Grafton County community in the White Mountains, according to the Boston Globe, and the shooting occurred at a junction used by local and through traffic. Fire crews blocked nearby roads while investigators secured the scene Thursday night, NHPR reported. The official accounts did not announce a continuing closure or evacuation, and authorities said there was no known continuing threat to the public.

The attorney general’s office and State Police Major Crime Unit will continue reconstructing the pursuit and the encounter. The next confirmed developments are likely to address the identity of the woman, the names and assignments of the officers, the sequence of the gunfire and whether any additional evidence changes the preliminary account. Until investigators release more information, the established facts are limited: the vehicle was being sought, the encounter ended in gunfire, the woman died at a hospital, and the circumstances remain under active investigation.
